text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Opposition Alliance For Democracy (AFORD) president Chakufwa Chihana on Saturday broke his long silence on the five-week-old civil servants strike and called for Malawi President Bakili Muluzi to intervene personally.

- Malaysia Prime Minister Mohathir Mohamad, on a three-day visit to Malawi, was questioned on Friday by his own press on when elections for their country's chief minister would be held after the constitutional 28 days had expired.
- Opposition parties have petitioned the High Court to declare results of a by-election in Blantyre city centre nul and void because of alleged fraud and corruption.
- Cabinet said government should spend 10.6 million kwacha to replace the entire fleet of vehicles for President Bakili Muluzi. No reason was given for replacing the fleet.

- Conditions of service for cabinet ministers were revised from April 1, with an additional new monthly allowance of 3,500 kwacha introduced for ministers who use personal accommodation when they are away from Lilongwe.
